paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: The line chart compares the performance of two methods—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minFDE₂₀ (in units of length, likely meters) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8 on the x-axis, which is labeled “Number of Examples” and uses a linear scale with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←)”, also uses a linear scale, spanning from 17 to 24, with tick marks at integer intervals. The ST-ES method is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, starting at a value of approximately 21.6 at 0 examples and decreasing to a value of approximately 17.2 at 8 examples, with a slight dip to 17.0 at 6 examples before recovering slightly. The Random method is represented by an orange line with circular markers, starting at approximately 24.0 at 0 examples and decreasing to approximately 21.7 at 8 examples, remaining relatively flat after the initial drop and showing a slight increase between 4 and 6 examples before stabilizing.
